title_tag: 10 Best Boat Tours in Dubai (2026): Speedboat vs Yacht
meta_description: Dubai speedboat tours and shared yacht cruises compared on price, route, food, swim stops and price per hour, from €16 to €80. Pick the right boat fast.
h1_main: 10 Best Boat Tours in Dubai in 2026
author_role: 10 speedboat tours and shared yacht cruises compared on price, route, length, food and price per hour
lead: For most visitors the best boat tour in Dubai is the 90-minute Marina, Palm and Burj Al Arab speedboat at €37: it reaches Ain Dubai, Atlantis and the Burj Al Arab with photo stops, from a boarding point inside Dubai Marina. On a tighter budget, a similar 90-minute speedboat costs €22.

The bigger decision is speedboat or yacht. Speedboats are open, fast and reach the Burj Al Arab in 90–100 minutes. Shared yachts are slower and steadier, some with an air-conditioned lower deck, with drinks included from €16–23 for an hour. The catch: the cheap 1-hour yacht loops stay around the Marina, Ain Dubai and JBR, and the Burj Al Arab and a BBQ usually come with the 2-hour options.

Below are 5 speedboats and 5 shared yachts, from a €16 hour on deck to an €80 three-hour swim cruise with a slide, BBQ lunch and unlimited drinks. Filter by boat type, route or budget, or jump to the comparison table.

review: This is the benchmark Dubai speedboat tour. For €37 you get 90 minutes on an open speedboat that runs out of Dubai Marina, up the coast past Ain Dubai and Jumeirah Beach, along the Palm Jumeirah to Atlantis and on to the Burj Al Arab, with photo stops at each one. That is every coastal landmark most visitors want, in one ride.

Compared with the cheaper speedboats below, the difference is the operator and the boarding point. Xclusive Yachts runs it from its own boarding point at Marina Level, Al Majara, the same base as its big shared yachts, and the guide stops the boat for photos rather than rushing past.

Two things to know. It is a sightseeing speedboat, not a thrill ride: the boat stops often, so if you want pure speed, look at a jet ski tour instead. And it is English only, with no food on board; you can bring cold snacks. Children under 5 cannot join.

review: If you want a yacht rather than a speedboat, start here. Xclusive Yachts runs shared cruises on yachts of 65 feet and up from Dubai Marina, and the cheapest slot is €23 for one hour with water and tropical drinks. You get an open upper deck, an air-conditioned lounge below and a waiting lounge with Wi-Fi before you board.

The option you pick decides the route. The 1-hour tour loops around Dubai Marina, Ain Dubai, JBR and Dubai Harbour; the longer sailings continue to the Palm, Atlantis and the Burj Al Arab and add a BBQ, while the morning option comes with a light breakfast. That makes it the most flexible yacht on the page, from a quick hour to a three-hour sunset BBQ.

Catches: alcohol is sold at the bar, there is no swim stop and swimwear is not allowed. Dress is smart casual, with no footwear on board. For an evening cruise built around dinner and shows instead, see our Dubai dinner cruises compared.

review: Same route as our #1, for €15 less. Splash Tours runs a 90-minute speedboat from behind the Al Rahim Mosque in Dubai Marina, out around the Palm Jumeirah, past Atlantis and on to the Burj Al Arab, returning past the royal palaces. At €22 that is about €15 per hour, the best hourly rate among the speedboats here.

The timetable is the other strength: departures run from 9:00 to 19:45, so you can fit a morning ride before a beach day or catch the sunset. Guests describe guides who stop at the landmarks and take photos for you, and a ride that really does speed between the stops.

What you give up against the #1 is the polish: the meeting point is by the Al Rahim Mosque on Al Seba Street rather than a branded boarding lounge, and there is only water on board. It is also not suitable for people with back problems, which matters on a bouncy open boat.

review: Sky Walker's shared yacht is the best alternative to our #2 if you would rather start at Dubai Harbour than inside the Marina. From €20 you board with welcome drinks, and soft drinks, juices and water are included on every option. The route runs through Dubai Marina, past Bluewaters and Ain Dubai and along Marina Beach, with the Burj Al Arab or Atlantis depending on the option you book.

The food is the reason to pick a longer slot. On the Burj 2-hour and 3-hour options the crew cooks a live BBQ on board: chicken and beef burgers, lamb kofta, chicken skewers, halloumi and vegetable skewers, fruit and muffins. A photographer and service staff are part of the crew.

Read the option names carefully: the 1-hour and 2-hour Atlantis Palm tours have no BBQ. Alcohol is bought at the bar, parking at the harbour costs AED 10 an hour and departures leave strictly on time. Routes depend on the weather, and in rough conditions not every landmark is visited. review: The Black Boats run only a couple of new BSK Marine speedboats with leather couch-style seats, and this 100-minute tour is their long route. It covers the Marina canal, Ain Dubai on Bluewaters, JBR and Skydive Dubai, both Atlantis The Palm and Atlantis The Royal, and finishes at the Burj Al Arab.

review: The cheapest way to get food included on a Dubai yacht. 360 Adventures sells three shared slots: a 1.5-hour cruise at 15:00 with a light meal, a 2-hour sunset cruise at 17:00 with light bites (BBQ in the cooler months) and a 20:00 option with BBQ dinner. Logistics need a little attention: the exact gate is sent by email or WhatsApp the day before or on the day, staff wear 360 Adventures T-shirts, and shoes come off before boarding. If you want a full sit-down dinner with entertainment instead, compare the options in our dinner cruise guide.

review: This is a different product from everything else on the page. Sky Walker's 3-hour Ride and Slide cruises from Dubai Harbour along the coast to a sheltered anchorage under the Palm Jumeirah, parks in a safe swimming zone and inflates the toys: a slide off the top deck, sea loungers, a paddle board and snorkelling gear.

At €80 it is the priciest option here, but it is also the only one where the price covers a full BBQ lunch and unlimited house drinks, cocktails and soft drinks. That works out at about €27 per hour, close to the 100-minute speedboat, with lunch and an open bar on top.

Set expectations right. You see the skyline, but this is not a landmark tour, and there is no Burj Al Arab. Most of the three hours is spent at anchor. For real underwater time, look at our Dubai scuba diving comparison. Bring swimwear, a towel and goggles.

review: For €16 this is the cheapest way onto a yacht in Dubai. Splash Tours, who also run our #3 speedboat, sail a shared yacht from behind the Al Rahim Mosque in Dubai Marina on a one-hour loop past Ain Dubai, Bluewaters Island and JBR, with tropical drinks and water on board.

It is the right pick when you are staying in the Marina and want an easy hour after dinner: guests recommend late-evening departures, when it is less crowded and the towers are lit, and say the crew takes photos and videos throughout.

What you do not get: the Palm, Atlantis or the Burj Al Arab, a live guide, or food. If those matter, our #2 from the same marina costs €7 more for its 1-hour option and scales up to BBQ and the Burj Al Arab.

Three numbers stand out. The Splash 90-minute speedboat at €15 per hour is the cheapest way to see the Burj Al Arab from the water. The Ride and Slide at €27 per hour costs about the same per hour as the premium 100-minute speedboat, but includes lunch, unlimited drinks and a swim. And for €16–23 a 1-hour yacht gets you drinks on deck but not the Palm or the Burj Al Arab.

• One boat tour, all the landmarks: the Marina, Palm and Burj Al Arab speedboat (€37, 90 minutes).
  • Same route, lowest price: the Splash 90-minute speedboat at €22, with departures from 9:00 to 19:45.
  • Couples who want comfort and few people on board: the 100-minute Black Boats tour, max 12 guests, leather seats.
  • A calm yacht with drinks, any age: the Dubai Marina yacht; book a 2-hour BBQ option if you want the Burj Al Arab.
  • Drinks covered and a live BBQ, from Dubai Harbour: the Dubai Harbour yacht; book the Burj 2-hour option for the BBQ.
  • Sunset with food for under €20: the sunset yacht with light bites, 17:00 departure.
  • Families who want to swim: the Ride and Slide yacht, the only shared cruise here with a swim stop.
  • Only an hour, or a non-English speaker in the group: the 1-hour Black Boats speedboat, guides in 5 languages.
  • A RIB ride with a choice of length: the RIB speedboat, 60 or 90 minutes.
  • Cheapest hour on the water: the 1-hour Marina yacht at €16.

Want more speed than a sightseeing boat gives you? Drive yourself with one of our best jet ski tours in Dubai. For the Palm from above rather than from the sea, compare the Dubai helicopter tours.

guide.h2: Speedboat vs Yacht Tour in Dubai
guide.html:
Speedboats (€20–43) are open boats with 1–1.5 hours on the water, photo stops at each landmark and bottled water. They are the faster way to reach the Burj Al Arab, but they bounce in choppy seas and most exclude young children (under 3 or under 5), pregnant women and people with back or heart problems. None serves food.

Shared yachts (€16–80) are slower and steadier, with an open upper deck, an air-conditioned lower deck on some boats (the Xclusive and sunset yachts) and soft or tropical drinks included. Food comes with specific options: breakfast or BBQ on the 2–3 hour sailings, light bites on the sunset slot, a full BBQ lunch on the swim cruise. Alcohol is extra on every yacht except the Ride and Slide, where house drinks are unlimited.

Rule of thumb: book a speedboat for landmarks and adrenaline, a yacht for sunset, drinks and mixed-age groups. In the hottest months the yacht's air-conditioned deck is the more comfortable choice.

guide.h2: Practical Tips: Timing, Dress Code and Getting There
guide.html:
Best time to go

Guests on three of the speedboats mention the 17:00 departure for the sunset. For an early start, the Splash speedboat runs from 9:00 and Xclusive offers a breakfast cruise. On the 1-hour Marina yacht, guests recommend late-evening slots as less crowded, with the towers lit.

What to bring and wear

Bring a passport or ID card (most operators ask for one), sunglasses and sunscreen. On the Xclusive speedboat wear flat shoes or sandals and light clothes. On the yachts, shoes come off before boarding, and Xclusive and Sky Walker ask for smart or summer casual with no bikinis; swimwear is only for the Ride and Slide, where you should also pack a towel and goggles.

Getting to the boat

None of the ten tours includes hotel pickup. In Dubai Marina there are three boarding points: Xclusive Yachts at Marina Level, Al Majara; Pier 7 on the Marina Promenade for The Black Boats; and behind the Al Rahim Mosque on Al Seba Street for Splash Tours. Sky Walker departs from Dubai Harbour Yacht Club, where parking costs AED 10 an hour. Arrive 15–30 minutes early: shared yachts leave on time and will not wait.

What costs extra

Alcohol on every shared yacht except the Ride and Slide, food on the 1-hour yacht options and the BBQ upgrades on longer sailings. For the city's main sights on land, see our Dubai city tours compared.

faqs.q: What is the best boat tour in Dubai?
faqs.a: For most visitors, the 90-minute Marina, Atlantis, Palm and Burj Al Arab speedboat at €37: it covers every major coastal landmark with photo stops. For a calmer cruise with drinks, the shared Dubai Marina yacht from €23 is the best yacht option.

faqs.q: Speedboat or yacht tour in Dubai: which is better?
faqs.a: A speedboat is better for landmarks and speed: it reaches the Burj Al Arab in 90–100 minutes for €22–43. A shared yacht is better for sunset, drinks and mixed-age groups, with an air-conditioned lower deck, but the cheap 1-hour yacht routes stay around the Marina, Ain Dubai and JBR.

faqs.q: How much does a boat tour in Dubai cost?
faqs.a: Shared boat tours start at €16 for a 1-hour yacht cruise in Dubai Marina. Speedboats cost from €20 for an hour and €22–43 for 90–100 minutes to the Burj Al Arab. A 3-hour yacht cruise with swimming, BBQ lunch and unlimited drinks costs €80.

faqs.q: Which Dubai boat tours go to the Burj Al Arab?
faqs.a: The 90-minute Xclusive and Splash speedboats, the 100-minute Black Boats tour and the 90-minute RIB option all reach the Burj Al Arab. On the yachts it comes with the longer options of the Xclusive and Sky Walker cruises. The sunset yacht goes to Atlantis or the Burj Al Arab depending on the sea.

faqs.q: Is food included on Dubai yacht tours?
faqs.a: On some options. The sunset yacht includes a light meal, light bites or BBQ dinner on every slot, the Ride and Slide includes a BBQ lunch, and the Xclusive and Sky Walker yachts include breakfast or BBQ only on their longer options. The 1-hour yachts serve drinks only. For a full dinner with shows, see our Dubai dinner cruises compared.

faqs.q: Can you swim on a Dubai boat tour?
faqs.a: Only on the Ride and Slide yacht cruise, which anchors in a swimming zone by the Palm with a slide, sea loungers, paddle board and snorkelling gear. The other shared yachts have no swim stop and do not allow swimwear, and the speedboats do not stop to swim.

faqs.q: Can I cancel a Dubai boat tour?
faqs.a: Yes. All ten tours on this page offer free cancellation up to 24 hours before departure, and all let you reserve now and pay later.

methodology: We compared 10 bookable Dubai boat tours: five shared speedboats and five shared, per-person yacht cruises from Dubai Marina and Dubai Harbour. Each was scored on from-price and price per hour, length, boat type, departure point, the landmarks on the route (Ain Dubai, JBR, the Palm and Atlantis, the Burj Al Arab), what food and drinks are really included, swim stops, group size and who it suits. Prices are live listing from-prices for a normal date; ratings come from verified guest reviews. Dinner cruises have their own comparison; private charters priced per group are not included.
